evidence.title: Correction algorithm for calculating heat transfer in air-cooling condenser based on analyzing steam condensation locations
evidence.abstract: ABSTRACT A correction algorithm based on analyzing the steam condensation locations is proposed to address the problem of large errors when calculating the heat transfer of the air-cooling condenser (ACC) in Fluent. By building a detailed geometric model of the ACC and using radiator boundary conditions to simplify the heat-sinking tube bundle, Fluent software was used to calculate the heat transfer of the ACC under four winter operating conditions, and then, the calculation results were further corrected by applying the correction algorithm. The results show that after using the correction algorithm, the errors between calculation results and experiment data are reduced from 4.20~36.98% to 0.01~1.79%. When the electric load of the air-cooling generator set or the ambient temperature was low, the condensation velocity increased, for which there would be a local steam-free area in the heat-sinking tube bundle of the ACC, leading to large errors when using the radiator model. At this point, the correction algorithm based on the analysis of steam condensation position can serve to improve the degree of accuracy. Meanwhile, this correction algorithm can be further expanded to use in the simulating calculation of an indirect air-cooling generator set, and it is able to correct the heat transfer calculation result of the air-cooling tower by analyzing the heat transfer condition of circulating water in the heat-sinking tube bundle, so that reliable data can be provided to guide the anti-freezing of the indirect air-cooling generator set.

evidence.title: Investigation of the performance of cold-end system in direct air-cooled power units under the influence of ambient winds
evidence.abstract:
Direct air-cooled condensers in power plants rely on heat transfer with the
 atmospheric environment to discharge thermal energy. The heat transfer
 process becomes complicated in practical operations when ambient wind is
 involved. To examine the impact of wind on the heat transfer performance of
 direct air-cooled condensers, this paper took into consideration three
 different wind directions, namely, headwind, crosswind and tailwind, as well
 as four different speeds (3 m/s, 6 m/s, 9 m/s, and 12 m/s), and numerically
 investigated their influences on the thermal performance of a 600 MW direct
 air-cooled power unit. The variation in ventilation rates and inlet air
 temperatures among the cells under the influence of ambient winds are also
 studied. Simulation results indicated that ambient winds induced thermal air
 recirculation and air backflow phenomena in the air-cooled island. The cells
 located on the windward side were significantly affected in all three wind
 direction conditions. The ventilation rates and inlet air temperatures among
 the cells were not uniform, showing an overall increasing trend. In
 particular, negative pressure zones were generated under tailwind
 conditions, severely impacting air flow rates at the fan inlet, and inlet
 air temperatures of cells. These phenomena became more pronounced with
 increasing wind speeds.

evidence.title: Explainable Boosting Machines for Thermal Load Prediction and Enclosure Thermodynamics of Residential HVAC Condensing Units
evidence.abstract: The architectural integration of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems in contemporary residential layouts increasingly subordinates thermodynamic performance to visual aesthetics, resulting in the concealment of outdoor split-system condensing units within louvered cabinets, service ducts, and constrained balcony alcoves. Such enclosures throttle the condenser airflow and, more damagingly, permit the exhaust plume to recirculate into the intake face, elevating the on-coil temperature above ambient and driving the vapour-compression cycle toward a high-lift, low-efficiency regime. Existing predictive models of this degradation are either computationally prohibitive, in the case of three-dimensional conjugate simulation, or opaque, in the case of deep and ensemble learners, and neither form yields the transparent, auditable relationships that building codes require. This work develops a framework based on Explainable Boosting Machines, a bagged and cyclically boosted realisation of generalized additive models with pairwise interactions. We first derive a closed-form cycle-level degradation law in which the compressor power admits a simple pole in a single dimensionless recirculation-resistance index, and we prove that the resulting physics is exactly representable as a second-order functional ANOVA decomposition in latent coordinates. This establishes that an additive learner with pairwise terms is not merely an interpretable approximation but the correct hypothesis class for the problem. A coupled computational fluid dynamics and lumped-parameter cycle model generates 15,000 parametric observations spanning frontal, lateral, and overhead clearances, louver porosity, ambient temperature, and part-load ratio. The learned model attains a mean absolute percentage error of 2.1% on held-out data, matching gradient-boosted tree and neural baselines while remaining fully decomposable. The extracted shape functions localise a sharp threshold in frontal clearance near 0.45 m, below which the contribution to compressor power accelerates in a manner consistent with the analytically predicted pole, and the leading pairwise term quantifies the porosity compensation required when that clearance cannot be met. The resulting relationships are stated as candidate clauses for residential energy codes.

evidence.title: Case study: The use of 'high-solidity' low noise axial fans to reduce noise from a rooftop air-handling unit
evidence.abstract: A case study was initiated with the aim of controlling the noise from axial (propeller type) condenser fans in an air-handling unit. The unit of concern was a 15 ton heating/cooling unit, with a pair of 30 inches diameter propeller fans used to move outdoor air over the condenser coil. It was found that the newer generation of `high-solidity' low-noise axial fans is an effective means of significantly reducing the noise impact of an existing rooftop air-handling unit.

evidence.title: Retrofit Pathways for HVAC Decarbonization: A sustainable solution for harnessing ultra-low-grade waste heat for energy efficiency and net-zero buildings
evidence.abstract:
Buildings are responsible for nearly one quarter of global energy consumption, with 30-50% of this demand arising from Heating, Ventilation and Air-Conditioning (HVAC) systems. While essential for ensuring indoor comfort, conventional vapor compression cycle (VCC) units reject a substantial share of ultra-low-grade heat (<80°C) to the urban environment. This not only represents a significant loss of useful energy but also contributes to local temperature rise and intensifies urban heat island effects, thereby driving further cooling demand. In this work, a retrofit-based strategy is proposed to integrate a single-stage organic Rankine cycle (SS-ORC) with the condenser of a conventional VCC system. A novel desuperheating-driven waste heat recovery approach, combined with an Adaptive Pinch Point (APP) method, is used to maximize the recoverable work potential under varying operating conditions. Multiple working fluid (WF) combinations are assessed, including low-GWP fluids (R1233zd (E), R1234ze (E), R1336mzz (Z)) for the VCC and zeotropic mixtures (R600/R600a and R365mfc/R152a) for the ORC. A comprehensive energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analysis is conducted to evaluate the performance and sustainability of the proposed system. Among the tested configurations, coupling R1234ze (E) in the VCC with R365mfc/R152a (0.1/0.9) in the ORC delivered the most favourable outcomes. This pair achieved a 3.76% enhancement in overall COP, and ORC exergy efficiency of 52.5%. From the economic standpoint, the system yielded the lowest levelized cost of electricity (0.061 US$/kWh) with a discounted payback period of only 3.8 years. Environmentally, the retrofit achieved an annual emission reduction of 70×10
 6
 kg of CO
 2
 / yr. Beyond technical and economic viability, the integration reduces heat rejection into the urban canopy, indirectly lowering surrounding cooling loads and improving the sustainability of indoor environments. The findings establish the proposed system as an effective and economically feasible retrofit method for enhancing energy efficiency and minimizing the carbon footprint of HVAC systems to support the energy conservation, net-zero transition and the sustainable built environment.

evidence.title: Analysis of joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device in summer
evidence.abstract: Abstract In view of the insufficient condensation capacity of air-cooling island in the summer, this paper proposed joint operation of air-cooling unit and peak cooling device to reduce the turbine back pressure. A joint operation cooling system can be formed by building a separate condenser room, retrofitting hydraulic pipe and adding a peak heat exchanger device. The influence factors on the air-cooling island condensation capacity are analyzed by establishing heat transfer calculation simulation model of the air-cooled condensers (ACCs) and the peak heat exchanger. The simulation results show that the main factor affecting the condensation capacity of air-cooling condenser and peak heat exchanger is ambient temperature, and the condensation capacity decreases significantly with increasing the ambient temperature. When it is hot in summer, the condensation capacity of original air-cooling system can not meet the demand, therefore, a joint operation scheme is determined for temperature above 10 °C: give priority to air-cooling system, peak cooling device as supplement when air-cooling system has insufficient condensation capacity. At the same time, the simulation results show that the joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device can effectively reduce turbine back pressure. In actual power plant, joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device was used at 25 °C and 30 °C under 330 MW, and the turbine back pressure decreased by 6.7 kPa and 6.1 kPa, respectively. The joint operation system has economic benefits and the investment payback period is 4 years.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Steam condensation location analysis reveals the presence of local vapor-free areas within the heat-sinking tube bundle under low electric load and low ambient temperature conditions, which invalidates standard radiator boundary models and creates high-error zones.
mechanism_map.intervention: Integrate a sensor array into the condenser coil to map local heat exchange rates and identify vapor-free zones in real-time; when low-load freezing risk is detected in these zones, automatically modulate the fan speed to create localized airflow stagnation zones that maintain coil surface temperature above 0°C, or activate a precise electrical bypass load to prevent the "steam-free" drop in local heat transfer.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Prevents the formation of ice on the coil sections where local heat transfer fails, thereby preventing the mechanical stress that cracks the refrigerant circuit and preserves the existing refrigerant charge.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: During a controlled shoulder-season low-load night, instrument the condenser with thermocouples at the predicted "steam-free" zones; if the intervention successfully prevents freezing, the temperature in these specific zones will remain above 0°C while the rest of the coil may be cooler, and no pressure spike indicating a blockage will occur.

It was found that the newer generation of `high-solidity' low-noise axial fans is an effective means of significantly reducing the noise impact of an existing rooftop air-handling unit.

system.value: Retrofit Pathways for HVAC Decarbonization: A sustainable solution for harnessing ultra-low-grade waste heat for energy efficiency and net-zero buildings

abstract.value:
Buildings are responsible for nearly one quarter of global energy consumption, with 30-50% of this demand arising from Heating, Ventilation and Air-Conditioning (HVAC) systems. While essential for ensuring indoor comfort, conventional vapor compression cycle (VCC) units reject a substantial share of ultra-low-grade heat (<80°C) to the urban environment. This not only represents a significant loss of useful energy but also contributes to local temperature rise and intensifies urban heat island effects, thereby driving further cooling demand. In this work, a retrofit-based strategy is proposed to integrate a single-stage organic Rankine cycle (SS-ORC) with the condenser of a conventional VCC system. A novel desuperheating-driven waste heat recovery approach, combined with an Adaptive Pinch Point (APP) method, is used to maximize the recoverable work potential under varying operating conditions. Multiple working fluid (WF) combinations are assessed, including low-GWP fluids (R1233zd (E), R1234ze (E), R1336mzz (Z)) for the VCC and zeotropic mixtures (R600/R600a and R365mfc/R152a) for the ORC. A comprehensive energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analysis is conducted to evaluate the performance and sustainability of the proposed system. Among the tested configurations, coupling R1234ze (E) in the VCC with R365mfc/R152a (0.1/0.9) in the ORC delivered the most favourable outcomes. This pair achieved a 3.76% enhancement in overall COP, and ORC exergy efficiency of 52.5%. From the economic standpoint, the system yielded the lowest levelized cost of electricity (0.061 US$/kWh) with a discounted payback period of only 3.8 years. Environmentally, the retrofit achieved an annual emission reduction of 70×10
 6
 kg of CO
 2
 / yr. Beyond technical and economic viability, the integration reduces heat rejection into the urban canopy, indirectly lowering surrounding cooling loads and improving the sustainability of indoor environments. The findings establish the proposed system as an effective and economically feasible retrofit method for enhancing energy efficiency and minimizing the carbon footprint of HVAC systems to support the energy conservation, net-zero transition and the sustainable built environment.

system.value: Analysis of joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device in summer

abstract.value: Abstract In view of the insufficient condensation capacity of air-cooling island in the summer, this paper proposed joint operation of air-cooling unit and peak cooling device to reduce the turbine back pressure. A joint operation cooling system can be formed by building a separate condenser room, retrofitting hydraulic pipe and adding a peak heat exchanger device. The influence factors on the air-cooling island condensation capacity are analyzed by establishing heat transfer calculation simulation model of the air-cooled condensers (ACCs) and the peak heat exchanger. The simulation results show that the main factor affecting the condensation capacity of air-cooling condenser and peak heat exchanger is ambient temperature, and the condensation capacity decreases significantly with increasing the ambient temperature. When it is hot in summer, the condensation capacity of original air-cooling system can not meet the demand, therefore, a joint operation scheme is determined for temperature above 10 °C: give priority to air-cooling system, peak cooling device as supplement when air-cooling system has insufficient condensation capacity. At the same time, the simulation results show that the joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device can effectively reduce turbine back pressure. In actual power plant, joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device was used at 25 °C and 30 °C under 330 MW, and the turbine back pressure decreased by 6.7 kPa and 6.1 kPa, respectively. The joint operation system has economic benefits and the investment payback period is 4 years.

Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
cemetery_warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

cemetery_warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:

A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Analysis of local thermal distribution identifies discrete "dry" zones (steam-free areas) in the heat-sinking tube bundle where the simplified radiator boundary condition fails; correcting the heat transfer model by mapping these specific locations prevents the overestimation of local heat capacity that masks coil freezing onset.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the uniform radiator boundary condition in the rooftop HVAC unit simulation with a spatially variable correction algorithm that identifies and excludes "frozen/ineffective" coil zones based on local condensation/heat-transfer position analysis.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Expansion of the correction algorithm to analyze the heat transfer condition of the circulating medium (refrigerant flow) within the heat-sinking tube bundle, allowing for the correction of heat transfer results in an indirect cooling context to guide anti-freezing strategies without altering the refrigerant inventory.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Integrate a circulating-fluid heat transfer analysis module into the control logic that corrects the air-cooling tower/condenser simulation by analyzing the local heat transfer condition of the refrigerant in the tube bundle, specifically targeting the "anti-freezing" guidance.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Application of a post-processing correction algorithm to the results of a detailed geometric model using simplified radiator boundary conditions, specifically targeting the reduction of errors caused by the mismatch between the simplified model and the actual heterogeneous condensation locations in winter/low-temperature conditions.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Implement a post-processing correction routine in the building management system that takes the output of the standard HVAC simulation (using simplified boundary conditions) and applies a location-based correction factor derived from analyzing condensation/heat transfer positions.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Spatial redistribution of thermal load via asymmetric tube geometry to eliminate "steam-free" (refrigerant-free) zones where condensation velocity is high, thereby maintaining uniform film thickness and preventing localized temperature drops below freezing point. (Domain: Heat transfer/hydrodynamics; Evidence: "When the electric load ... was low, the condensation velocity increased, for which there would be a local steam-free area ... leading to large errors")
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Replace the standard uniform circular tube bundle with a staggered arrangement of variable-diameter tubes where the diameter is progressively increased from the inlet to the outlet, ensuring the local cross-sectional flow velocity does not exceed the threshold for film rupture.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Active geometric modulation of airflow impingement angles to prevent stagnation zones and ensure even heat rejection, based on the principle that correcting calculation errors requires analyzing the position of heat transfer conditions. (Domain: Fluid dynamics/CFD correlation; Evidence: "correction algorithm based on the analysis of steam condensation position can serve to improve the degree of accuracy")
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Installation of variable-pitch guide vanes and a non-uniform fan shroud geometry in front of the condenser coil that dynamically adjusts the local Nusselt number distribution, preventing high-velocity air jets from bypassing the coldest (inlet) tubes and striking the warmest (outlet) tubes during low-load conditions.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Geometric isolation of the high-risk low-load section via physical partitioning, allowing the system to operate in a "corrected" regime where only a portion of the heat sink is active, thereby preventing the "large errors" associated with the full radiator model under low thermal load. (Domain: Modular heat exchanger design; Evidence: "correct the heat transfer calculation result ... by analyzing the heat transfer condition ... so that reliable data can be provided to guide the anti-freezing")
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Division of the condenser coil into two physically separated sections (primary and auxiliary) with independent airflow dampers, where the geometric arrangement forces all refrigerant to flow through the smaller primary section during low-load night conditions, effectively downscaling the heat sink surface area to match the reduced refrigerant load.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Ambient wind impingement creates non-uniform ventilation rates and inlet air temperature gradients across the condenser coil array, causing localized stagnation zones where convective heat transfer is insufficient to maintain coil surface temperature above the freezing point during low-load operation.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Reorient the rooftop unit's primary air intake axis to align with the prevailing tailwind direction and install static baffles on the windward face to disrupt recirculation.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Tailwind conditions generate negative pressure zones at the fan inlet, reducing airflow rate and increasing inlet air temperature, which paradoxically reduces the heat rejection capacity required to keep the coil warm; however, the reduction in mass flow velocity increases the thermal boundary layer thickness, causing localized stagnation and freezing in the low-velocity core of the stream.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Design the fan intake cowl to generate a localized positive pressure zone that counteracts the tailwind-induced negative pressure, decoupling the internal airflow from the external wind shear layer.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: The non-uniform distribution of ventilation rates among the condenser cells results in some sections operating at sub-critical Reynolds numbers for effective heat transfer, allowing the refrigerant temperature to drop below the dew point of ambient humidity; this is driven by the wind-induced disparity where "ventilation rates and inlet air temperatures among the cells were not uniform."
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Segment the condenser coil into isolated "cells" with individual fan compartments and inter-cell thermal bypass channels, allowing air to redistribute from high-flow (windward) cells to low-flow (leeward/stagnant) cells to homogenize the temperature field.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Thermodynamic mitigation via head-pressure control; maintaining a minimum condensing pressure/temperature ensures the evaporator temperature remains above freezing despite low ambient conditions and part-load operation.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Implement a minimum head-pressure control loop using a condenser fan cycling controller or a variable-speed condenser fan motor to reduce airflow and maintain condenser pressure.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Thermal isolation via circuit decoupling; stopping refrigerant flow to the condenser coil prevents heat removal from the coil fins, allowing them to remain at ambient temperature rather than dropping below freezing point.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Install a solenoid valve on the liquid line or a condenser isolation valve that closes when the system detects low head pressure or high coil surface humidity/icing risk, isolating the condenser coil from the active refrigerant circuit.

hypothesis_attribution.mechanism: Mechanical mitigation via airflow disruption; preventing the formation of a stable ice layer by disrupting the boundary layer or physically removing ice before it reaches critical thickness/weight that causes mechanical stress cracking.
hypothesis_attribution.intervention: Install a condenser coil de-icing fan array or a mechanical coil combing system that activates based on differential pressure across the coil or time-based cycling to prevent ice buildup on the fins.

CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.justification: R377 patent-text ground truth (TOSCANINI/R377_PATENT_TEXT_FETCH.json + R377_PATENT_TEXT_GROUND_TRUTH.json): 12/30 family representatives (40%) were substantively irrelevant cross-domain term collisions (CWDM optical link for a battery-thermal candidate; dental-condition monitoring for rolling stock; bone fracture forceps for rail steel...). A hit sharing NO entity term with the candidate now needs >= 3 NON-generic mechanism terms to be mechanism art: the measured true cross-domain analog (line-pipe steel with hydrogen fracture toughness for a rail-steel candidate) shares 3 non-generic terms and survives; every measured false positive shares <= 2 and is demoted. This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).
CROSS_DOMAIN_MIN_NONGENERIC_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap remains a proxy; entity word-sense collisions ('gear': steering vs draft) can still pass — disclosed limitation, not a solved problem

MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.justification: same term-overlap rule family as the pipeline relevance adjudicator and the Q2 instrument (>= 2 shared content terms = domain-specific rather than accidental collision); NOT weakened relative to any prior gate
MIN_MECHANISM_OVERLAP.uncertainty: term overlap is a proxy for mechanism identity

ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.justification: a family ANTICIPATES only when nearly ALL elements of the candidate's FULL distinguishing set (uncapped — the claim elements, not the 6-term query core) appear in the family's claim/abstract text; 0.8 leaves a >= 20% element margin — anything lower would convert partial art into a kill (Art. XXVIII forbids). Measured adversarial case: a domain-only patent reached 0.857 against a capped denominator whose true differentiators (acoustic, multi-modal) had been ranked out
ANTICIPATION_COVERAGE_RATIO.uncertainty: claim coverage measured by term overlap, not a claim chart; recorded per family with evidence tier

A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM (sharpened per CEO Round 56o): 'Existing information + existing transformation + existing control, merely recombined, is insufficient. A combination qualifies only if it produces a demonstrably new technical effect that survives prior art and non-obviousness attack. A world-class invention needs a genuinely new technical information source, transformation, or control capability. Do not build an AI layer on top of an already-claimed sensing/control architecture.' warnings.lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.lesson: Any anti-fouling mechanism that relies on flow direction must be tested against RETROGRADE flow. Retrograde flow is a realistic clinical scenario (cough, Valsalva, venous pressure changes).

informational.mechanism: M3_REFINED electrothermal SMA retrieval
informational.lesson: ALWAYS report worst-case reliability for clinical devices. Averages mask catastrophic failure modes. Thermal activation in a 37°C body environment has a narrow window (37-45°C = 8°C max). Sensor electronics are a SPOF that cannot be fully resolved by redundancy (common-mode failures).

informational.mechanism: M5_REFINED adaptive over-drainage controller (sleep-state + venous pressure)
informational.lesson: Do not assume VP shunt problems apply to the eShunt. The eShunt's drainage geometry is fundamentally different (short path, no siphon). Always verify the problem exists for the SPECIFIC device geometry. Over-drainage is siphon-driven; without a hydrostatic column, it may not occur.

informational.mechanism: Flow reversal obstruction clearing (R3)
informational.lesson: Retrograde flush for eShunt pushes debris toward brain. The eShunt venous drainage direction makes retrograde more dangerous than VP shunts (peritoneal). However, the clinical hazard is ANALOGICAL (SAH blood causes inflammation), not directly proven for shunt debris. MODEL_DERIVED + ANALOGICAL_EVIDENCE — not PROVEN_UNSAFE.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: ABSTRACT A correction algorithm based on analyzing the steam condensation locations is proposed to address the problem of large errors when calculating the heat transfer of the air-cooling condenser (ACC) in Fluent. By building a detailed geometric model of the ACC and using radiator boundary conditions to simplify the heat-sinking tube bundle, Fluent software was used to calculate the heat transfer of the ACC under four winter operating conditions, and then, the calculation results were further corrected by applying the correction algorithm. The results show that after using the correction algorithm, the errors between calculation results and experiment data are reduced from 4.20~36.98% to 0.01~1.79%. When the electric load of the air-cooling generator set or the ambient temperature was low, the condensation velocity increased, for which there would be a local steam-free area in the heat-sinking tube bundle of the ACC, leading to large errors when using the radiator model. At this point, the correction algorithm based on the analysis of steam condensation position can serve to improve the degree of accuracy. Meanwhile, this correction algorithm can be further expanded to use in the simulating calculation of an indirect air-cooling generator set, and it is able to correct the heat transfer calculation result of the air-cooling tower by analyzing the heat transfer condition of circulating water in the heat-sinking tube bundle, so that reliable data can be provided to guide the anti-freezing of the indirect air-cooling generator set.

Direct air-cooled condensers in power plants rely on heat transfer with the
 atmospheric environment to discharge thermal energy. The heat transfer
 process becomes complicated in practical operations when ambient wind is
 involved. To examine the impact of wind on the heat transfer performance of
 direct air-cooled condensers, this paper took into consideration three
 different wind directions, namely, headwind, crosswind and tailwind, as well
 as four different speeds (3 m/s, 6 m/s, 9 m/s, and 12 m/s), and numerically
 investigated their influences on the thermal performance of a 600 MW direct
 air-cooled power unit. The variation in ventilation rates and inlet air
 temperatures among the cells under the influence of ambient winds are also
 studied. Simulation results indicated that ambient winds induced thermal air
 recirculation and air backflow phenomena in the air-cooled island. The cells
 located on the windward side were significantly affected in all three wind
 direction conditions. The ventilation rates and inlet air temperatures among
 the cells were not uniform, showing an overall increasing trend. In
 particular, negative pressure zones were generated under tailwind
 conditions, severely impacting air flow rates at the fan inlet, and inlet
 air temperatures of cells. These phenomena became more pronounced with
 increasing wind speeds.

custody_records.raw_content: The architectural integration of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems in contemporary residential layouts increasingly subordinates thermodynamic performance to visual aesthetics, resulting in the concealment of outdoor split-system condensing units within louvered cabinets, service ducts, and constrained balcony alcoves. Such enclosures throttle the condenser airflow and, more damagingly, permit the exhaust plume to recirculate into the intake face, elevating the on-coil temperature above ambient and driving the vapour-compression cycle toward a high-lift, low-efficiency regime. Existing predictive models of this degradation are either computationally prohibitive, in the case of three-dimensional conjugate simulation, or opaque, in the case of deep and ensemble learners, and neither form yields the transparent, auditable relationships that building codes require. This work develops a framework based on Explainable Boosting Machines, a bagged and cyclically boosted realisation of generalized additive models with pairwise interactions. We first derive a closed-form cycle-level degradation law in which the compressor power admits a simple pole in a single dimensionless recirculation-resistance index, and we prove that the resulting physics is exactly representable as a second-order functional ANOVA decomposition in latent coordinates. This establishes that an additive learner with pairwise terms is not merely an interpretable approximation but the correct hypothesis class for the problem. A coupled computational fluid dynamics and lumped-parameter cycle model generates 15,000 parametric observations spanning frontal, lateral, and overhead clearances, louver porosity, ambient temperature, and part-load ratio. The learned model attains a mean absolute percentage error of 2.1% on held-out data, matching gradient-boosted tree and neural baselines while remaining fully decomposable. The extracted shape functions localise a sharp threshold in frontal clearance near 0.45 m, below which the contribution to compressor power accelerates in a manner consistent with the analytically predicted pole, and the leading pairwise term quantifies the porosity compensation required when that clearance cannot be met. The resulting relationships are stated as candidate clauses for residential energy codes.

custody_records.raw_content: A case study was initiated with the aim of controlling the noise from axial (propeller type) condenser fans in an air-handling unit. The unit of concern was a 15 ton heating/cooling unit, with a pair of 30 inches diameter propeller fans used to move outdoor air over the condenser coil. It was found that the newer generation of `high-solidity' low-noise axial fans is an effective means of significantly reducing the noise impact of an existing rooftop air-handling unit.

custody_records.raw_content:
Buildings are responsible for nearly one quarter of global energy consumption, with 30-50% of this demand arising from Heating, Ventilation and Air-Conditioning (HVAC) systems. While essential for ensuring indoor comfort, conventional vapor compression cycle (VCC) units reject a substantial share of ultra-low-grade heat (<80°C) to the urban environment. This not only represents a significant loss of useful energy but also contributes to local temperature rise and intensifies urban heat island effects, thereby driving further cooling demand. In this work, a retrofit-based strategy is proposed to integrate a single-stage organic Rankine cycle (SS-ORC) with the condenser of a conventional VCC system. A novel desuperheating-driven waste heat recovery approach, combined with an Adaptive Pinch Point (APP) method, is used to maximize the recoverable work potential under varying operating conditions. Multiple working fluid (WF) combinations are assessed, including low-GWP fluids (R1233zd (E), R1234ze (E), R1336mzz (Z)) for the VCC and zeotropic mixtures (R600/R600a and R365mfc/R152a) for the ORC. A comprehensive energy, exergy, economic and environmental (4E) analysis is conducted to evaluate the performance and sustainability of the proposed system. Among the tested configurations, coupling R1234ze (E) in the VCC with R365mfc/R152a (0.1/0.9) in the ORC delivered the most favourable outcomes. This pair achieved a 3.76% enhancement in overall COP, and ORC exergy efficiency of 52.5%. From the economic standpoint, the system yielded the lowest levelized cost of electricity (0.061 US$/kWh) with a discounted payback period of only 3.8 years. Environmentally, the retrofit achieved an annual emission reduction of 70×10
 6
 kg of CO
 2
 / yr. Beyond technical and economic viability, the integration reduces heat rejection into the urban canopy, indirectly lowering surrounding cooling loads and improving the sustainability of indoor environments. The findings establish the proposed system as an effective and economically feasible retrofit method for enhancing energy efficiency and minimizing the carbon footprint of HVAC systems to support the energy conservation, net-zero transition and the sustainable built environment.

custody_records.raw_content: Abstract In view of the insufficient condensation capacity of air-cooling island in the summer, this paper proposed joint operation of air-cooling unit and peak cooling device to reduce the turbine back pressure. A joint operation cooling system can be formed by building a separate condenser room, retrofitting hydraulic pipe and adding a peak heat exchanger device. The influence factors on the air-cooling island condensation capacity are analyzed by establishing heat transfer calculation simulation model of the air-cooled condensers (ACCs) and the peak heat exchanger. The simulation results show that the main factor affecting the condensation capacity of air-cooling condenser and peak heat exchanger is ambient temperature, and the condensation capacity decreases significantly with increasing the ambient temperature. When it is hot in summer, the condensation capacity of original air-cooling system can not meet the demand, therefore, a joint operation scheme is determined for temperature above 10 °C: give priority to air-cooling system, peak cooling device as supplement when air-cooling system has insufficient condensation capacity. At the same time, the simulation results show that the joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device can effectively reduce turbine back pressure. In actual power plant, joint operation of air-cooling system and peak cooling device was used at 25 °C and 30 °C under 330 MW, and the turbine back pressure decreased by 6.7 kPa and 6.1 kPa, respectively. The joint operation system has economic benefits and the investment payback period is 4 years.
